title: Balisacan: AI can fight corruption, monitor projects, speed up government
summary: The Marcos Jr. administration plans to harness artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline government processes, monitor infrastructure projects, and help fight corruption as it prepares a governance…

blocks.text: The Marcos Jr. administration plans to harness artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline government processes, monitor infrastructure projects, and help fight corruption as it prepares a governance framework for the rapidly evolving technology, according to the country ’s chief economist. Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan told reporters last week that AI could be deployed across critical public sectors, including education, health, and infrastructure, to improve government efficiency and accelerate the delivery of public services. Balisacan identified project monitoring as among the most practical applications of AI, particularly in tracking infrastructure development and ensuring projects are completed on time. The DEPDev chief said AI could also be applied to public-private partnership (PPP) projects. He said automating government processes through AI could also strengthen efforts against corruption. The AI governance framework is “more or less finished,” Balisacan said, with its formal release possibly this month, depending on President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s schedule. He said the President could still propose changes to make the framework more workable and flexible as the government seeks to use AI as a tool for development. The framework builds on the National AI Strategy of the Philippines (NAIS-PH), which the government approved in May 2025. The government’s push to integrate AI into its operations forms part of a broader effort to harness the technology to raise productivity and support economic development while preparing Filipino workers and industries for the disruptions it could bring. Balisacan earlier said fears that AI could cause massive job losses in the country’s information technology and business process management (IT-BPM) industry may be overstated, as the sector continues to expand despite the rapid adoption of the technology. Speaking at the Economic Journalists Association of the Philippines (EJAP) Economic Forum last month, Balisacan identified innovation and productivity as major sources of economic growth and stressed the need to upskill the Filipino workforce to adapt to emerging technologies such as AI. The DEPDev chief also pointed to the proposed Pax Silica development in New Clark City as an opportunity to diversify the economy by attracting investments that support industrialization and higher-value activities. The government, however, faces challenges in building the foundations needed to maximize the economic benefits of AI. Manila Bulletin reported earlier the World Bank ’s warning that weak and fragmented data systems could hold back the country’s AI ambitions and recommended the formulation of a cohesive government data strategy identifying the investments needed in data, infrastructure, and people. The proposed strategy could form part of the data pillar of the AI governance framework being developed under the National Innovation Council (NIC), with DEPDev among the lead agencies. Beyond government operations, Balisacan has identified potential AI applications in the energy sector to optimize power grids while promoting greener and more efficient operations. He also sees AI-enabled assistive technologies playing a role in healthcare and social inclusion as the country’s population ages. Balisacan has also stressed the importance of expanding the country’s digital infrastructure through initiatives such as eGovPH, the national fiber backbone, satellite internet, and the Konektadong Pinoy Act. He has likewise emphasized the need for ethical and trustworthy AI use, including adherence to Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)-Civil Service Commission (CSC) guidelines on responsible AI use in government to uphold transparency and accountability.
